brief: GS's Adam Crook compiles cross-desk views ahead of a volatile Thanksgiving week. Callahan: NDX/SOX/Info Tech are oversold, valuations at over-10-year lows, but faded year-end-rally hope and the absence of a clear catalyst have produced a buyers' strike even as fundamentals (KEYS/NVDA/PANW beats) hold up; chart-implied semiconductor earnings cuts are not shared by most investors, who expect upward revisions into DELL/MU/AVGO/HPE prints. Miller and Morgan describe the 2018 drawdown analog going mainstream, positioning washed out to multi-year/10-year lows, hedge funds selling tech at a record pace, and a US vol panic index at 9.2/10 (relief has historically followed readings above 9.5). Hammond, Snider and Wilson debate where earnings growth comes from next: decelerating AI capex growth argues the best infrastructure-stock returns are behind, so GS recommends owning hyperscalers instead, citing accelerating cloud growth and $1.8tn in backlog; the offsetting risk is cracks in AI financing and a peaking investment impulse. Privorotsky flags a hawkish Fed (Waller backing 50bp in December) against hot jobs and CPI data, leaving core PCE, the jobs report and the December Fed meeting as the next catalysts. Makkar and Fenina see favorable AI-semis risk/reward and prefer SNDK over MU, STX over WDC, and are Buy-rated on SITM, MCHP, ADI and NXPI.
